newsitem.title: CANADA: Westcoast to add B.C. natgas processing.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast to add B.C. natgas processing.

text.p: Westcoast Energy Inc said on Monday it planned to build a new natural gas plant in the Highway area of northeast British Columbia and expand its under-construction Jedney plant in the province.
Both projects, located in the Fort St. John area, were estimated to cost over C$100 million, Westcoast said.

The company said its field services division planned to build an 80 million cubic feet per day plant at Highway, which would serve a number of producers operating in the Wargen, Birley, Silver, Lapp, Redeye and Dahl areas of northeast B.C.
The Highway project, which would be in service by May 1997, would also include about 90 km of gathering pipelines. The project's cost was estimated at C$47 million.
Westcoast said it would double the capacity of its Jedney gas plant to 140 MMCFD in a C$60 million expansion project.
Jedney, which is under construction 180 km north of Fort St. John and was scheduled to start operations in November, would now also begin processing in May 1997.
The plant was being built to serve producers in the Tommy Lakes and Conroy regions.
Westcoast field services president Irv Koop said the company would apply to the B.C. government for project approvals in the next week.
"We are determined to meet the needs of our customers, both upstream and downstream, in a timely and competitive manner," Koop said in a statement. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
